newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end modestly up, market selective.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end modestly up, market selective.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended modestly higher on Thursday, with Henderson Land's solid fiscal 1996 earnings and overnight gains on Wall Street unable to arouse enthusiasm in a selective market, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index rose 15.36 points to 11,251.72. Turnover was HK$4.41 billion compared to K$3.74 billion on Wednesday.
"Today is more a market of stocks than a stock market," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia.
He said action in the major blue chips had been selective, with Henderson Land rising HK$0.75 to HK$61.75, following its 1995/96 results, but other property developers weak.
Henderson Investment fell HK$0.20 to HK$7.95 after disappointing fiscal 1996 results but other property investment companies made gains.
Henderson Land posted fiscal 1996 net profit of HK$8.36 billion compared to HK$7.03 billion and its Henderson Investment unit reported profit of HK$1.89 billion versus HK$1.63 billion.
Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage, said investors were sceptical of Wall Street's strength ahead of the release of August U.S. producer price data later on Thursday.
The Dow industrials rose 27.74 points to 5,754.92 on Wednesday.
"I think they are just being wary because they can't believe Wall Street is pushing up to a record again and that the market could be so strong ahead of an interest rate increase," he said.
"Henderson's figures, as good as they were, seemed to be largely discounted," Gorges added.

However, he said underlying sentiment in the market appeared to be positive and pointed to the strong response to casual weak maker and retailer Glorious Sun's initial public offering. The company said the IPO was 236 times subscribed.

"The market coud push up to around 11,500 (points) but it needs a little bit of steam or news to get it going," said Gorges. "Data showing a slowdown in the States or that inflation is subdued might give the market a bit more encouragement."
Among the property developers, Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.25 to HK$76.25 and Hysan was off HK$0.05 to HK$23.35.
In the property investment sector, Wharf rose HK$0.10 to HK$30.00 and Amoy Properties added HK$0.15 to HK$8.95.
HSBC Holdings ended the session strong, rising HK$1.00 to HK$135.50. Swire Pacific rose HK$0.93 to HK$68.75.
Hongkong Telecom fell HK$0.15 to HK$12.70
